task.title: naturalsize keeps the fraction of non-integer byte counts below the base
task.body:
Why: https://github.com/python-humanize/humanize/issues/459 ; src/humanize/filesize.py:94-98 truncates with int(). On b519e48 `naturalsize(1.5)` returns '1 Bytes' and `naturalsize(1.9, gnu=True)` returns '1B', while `naturalsize(1500)` keeps '1.5 kB'.
Outcome: `humanize.naturalsize(value, binary=False, gnu=False, format="%.1f")` with a finite non-integral float whose absolute value is below the base (1000, or 1024 with `binary` or `gnu`) formats the number with `format` and always uses the plural unit: `naturalsize(1.5) == '1.5 Bytes'`, `naturalsize(0.5) == '0.5 Bytes'`, `naturalsize(-1.5) == '-1.5 Bytes'`, `naturalsize(1.5, gnu=True) == '1.5B'`, `naturalsize(1.5, binary=True) == '1.5 Bytes'`. Integral input is unchanged: `naturalsize(1) == '1 Byte'`, `naturalsize(300) == '300 Bytes'`, `naturalsize(300.0) == '300 Bytes'`, `naturalsize(0) == '0 Bytes'`, `naturalsize(1, gnu=True) == '1B'`, and `naturalsize(1500) == '1.5 kB'`. The two existing cases in tests/test_filesize.py that expect `naturalsize(1.1) == '1 Bytes'` and `naturalsize(1.1, gnu=True) == '1B'` pin the old truncation; they change to '1.1 Bytes' and '1.1B'.
Proof: add tests to tests/test_filesize.py for the values above.

install: python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -q babel -e '.[tests]' && .venv/bin/pybabel --quiet compile --directory src/humanize/locale --domain humanize
